description.narrative: RESLOG 2 (Resilience in Local Governance 2) is a local governance project to be implemented in Lebanon and Turkey with funding from the Regional Strategy for the Syrian crisis. RESLOG 2 is planned for an implementation period of 32 months, with a planned starting date in May 2022, and a budget of SEK 80 000 000 incl. of VAT. The geographical scope is similar to the previous phase RESLOG 1 with key partners being Unions of Municipalities and its members in Akkar governorate in Lebanon and in Marmara and Cukorova in Turkey

RESLOG 2 (Resilience in Local Governance 2) är ett lokalt styrningsprojekt som ska implementeras i Libanon och Turkiet med finansiering från den Regionala Strategin för Syrienkrisen. RESLOG 2 är planerad för en implementeringsperiod på 32 månader, med planerat startdatum i maj 2022, och en budget på 80 000 000 SEK inkl. moms. Den geografiska omfattningen liknar den tidigare fasen RESLOG 1, med nyckelpartners som kommunförbund och deras medlemmar i Akkar guvernement i Libanon, och i Marmara och Cukorova i Turkiet

The impact goal of RESLOG 2 was defined as: Selected municipalities in Akkar, Lebanon and in Türkiye have become more resilient through strengthened municipal governance, including improved abilities to provide more equal access to services, livelihood opportunities and means for peaceful co-habitation to women and men from Syrian refugee and local communities.
The three overall outcomes contributing to the impact goal were:
1) Strengthen provision of municipal services and peaceful cohabitation through fostering of active citizenship;
2) More decent and greener local livelihood opportunities for women and men in refugee and local communities;
3) Turkish local government actors have become more systematic and effective in contributing to migration policy matters of concern (only Türkiye).
The three outcomes were further operationalised through six intermediate outcomes.
A component was added in 2023 (Agreement Amendment no. 3). The objective of the component was to strengthen the ability of Turkish municipalities to take a leading role in the reconstruction work on a local level, following the devastating earthquakes in Türkiye in February 2023.
A new component was also added in late 2024, expanding the Crisis Management units to more Unions of Municipalities, and accordingly extending the project for four months.

RESLOG 2 has contributed to increased capacity to create a more sustainable situation for refugees and host communities in Lebanon and Türkiye. In both countries, municipalities and unions of municipalities partnering with SALAR have shown increased capacity for data collection, which has been used for analyses leading to evidence based planning and decision making. Below are some examples of activities and results in the two countries.
In Türkiye, there has been a capacity development process focused on how to handle socio-economic data within migration planning, including how to mainstream gender perspectives. Turkish municipalities that participated in the capacity development process subsequently used this for example to identify how refugee women and girls could be more fully included in the services offered at municipal level.
During the course of the contribution, tools such as "migration master plans" were introduced. Migration master plans have according to SALAR's final report continued to be used by many of the Turkish municipalities and contributes to migration related objectives being included in the municipalities' strategic plans. For example, in Mersin, SALAR supported a broadened municipal migration planning process which included Syrian and Turkish civil society organisations. SALAR assessed that this had positive effects on social cohesion.
During 2025, RESLOG supported capacity development for Syrian civil society organisations, through which the organisations gained increased understanding of Turkish municipalities and how they cooperate with civil society. Through RESLOG 2, SALAR saw increased cooperation between Turkish municipalities and Syrian civil society organisations. This made it easier for Turkish municipalities to reach Syrian inhabitants.
SALAR assesses that RESLOG 2 has contributed to increased dialogue on migration both between municipalities and unions of municipalities in Türkiye, and with central authorities. An annual forum was created through which national and local authorities can meet to discuss migration issues. When the Union of Municipalities of Türkiye (UMT) held its first council meeting after the local elections in 2025, the new leader of UMT conveyed proposals from a policy paper on migration which had been developed within the framework of RESLOG 2, and these proposals subsequently received attention on a national level.
In Lebanon, participating municipalities have gained new tools to analyse needs and implement efficient planning. More specifically, such tools are related to digitalisation, a GIS-system, the collections of socio-economic data and capacity development regarding gender related analysis. A concrete example of results was seen when two unions of municipalities received a request for information about the needs of winterization support for Syrian households in 2024. The union of municipalities that participated in RESLOG 2 could share relevant and gender disaggregated data within 24 hours. Meanwhile, the non-participating union of municipalities needed two weeks to provide the corresponding information.
A further positive development is that in 2025, some of the Lebanese municipalities conducted an updated data collection exercise which included new GIS maps and satellite images. As a result of this, 69 municipalities in North Lebanon got access to a digital data package which can form a foundation for the planning of policies and concrete measures.
Furthermore, within the framework of RESLOG 2, municipalities have also established units for crisis management called "First Response Teams". These include both men and women, Lebanese and Syrians, and have contributed to social cohesion within the municipalities.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
